title: Product label boundary
text: Do not provide pesticide product names, rates, tank mixes, intervals, or crop-stage restrictions as final advice without the current label, crop and site, target pest, jurisdiction, application method, and relevant weather constraints. If context is missing, answer at mode-of-action, stewardship, and diagnostic level.

title: Label version and jurisdiction boundary
text: Product labels and registrations vary by country, state or province, crop, pest, timing, formulation, and label version. RAG records for labels must carry retrieval date, label version, jurisdiction, source URL or document identifier, and allowed-use scope.

title: Fertility rate boundary
text: Do not give final fertilizer rates without crop, realistic yield goal, recent soil test with method and units, sampling depth, pH, organic matter, previous crop, manure or compost credits, irrigation or drainage context, and local calibration. When data are missing, provide a checklist and decision workflow.

title: Soil-test method and unit boundary
text: Soil-test values are method-specific. Bray, Olsen, Mehlich, ammonium acetate, DTPA, nitrate-N, and other methods should not be treated as interchangeable without calibration. Always preserve units, depth, extraction method, and lab reference range.

title: Field-data prescription boundary
text: A variable-rate or field-data prescription should not be generated from raw layers alone. It needs boundary validation, projection alignment, cleaned yield/as-applied data, outlier handling, soil-test support, management-zone rationale, human review, and an audit trail.

title: Regulated advice audit record
text: For product, nutrient, or prescription advice, save the inputs used, missing inputs, retrieved sources, tool outputs, assumptions, and confidence boundaries. An agronomy agent should make review easier, not erase professional accountability.
